goal: Security review of SquidCloud encryption keys + design an internal API layer; two read-only audits completed.
goal_source: interactive query from human (404 on squidcloud-cluster legacy chunk downloads; deprecate deepread/books UI)
last_actions: 2026-11-24: Launched two read-only audits (client key handling; Supabase DB/functions) plus independent repo/CLI checks.

CLIENT: default managed uploads escrow raw AES key to server (file-key/store-file-key) with KEK from SQUIDVEIL_MASTER_KEY - NOT zero-knowledge; false docs claims. store-file-key failure writes raw key into files.tags (res54.ts:782-791), which get_shared_file_info returns to anon. file-key bypasses PREL/f2fa for JWT holders (132-143). Markdown preview uses weak blocklist sanitizer + dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

SUPABASE CRITICAL (live): shares RLS policy returns ALL public share rows incl shared_encryption_key + access_code; get_shared_file_info / get_file_for_share are anon-callable SECURITY DEFINER key/path oracles with no password check; update_share_options lets anon overwrite any share; get_secret is anon-callable vault reader; files bucket public; anon has EXECUTE on kza_prel token-signing primitives; several key functions verify_jwt=false; hardcoded backfill token.
VERIFIED OK: profile is_admin/tier NOT user-writable; github_connections token RLS owner-only; file_key_vault scoped; file-key JWT path guarded. No changes made - read-only.
Proposed phased plan: Phase 0 SQL containment (revoke grants/policies), Phase 1 BFF with HttpOnly cookies, Phase 2 user-held key hierarchy for true E2E.

2026-11-24: Wrote design doc docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-full-e2e-redesign-design.md; independent reviewer found 8 blockers (contradictory key hierarchy, unsafe migration, PRF salt/per-credential issue, BFF raw-key exposure, share password leak, incomplete Phase 0, missing AAD/nonce discipline). Rewrote as v2 fixing all blockers; 2 open decisions remain for the human.

2026-11-24: User clarified target UX = iCloud/Google Drive. Noted GDrive is not E2E; rewrote design v3 around iCloud Advanced Data Protection: device keystore keys, new-device approval from existing device, recovery key fallback, ciphertext sync while locked, no server KEK.

2026-11-24: User asked for wallet-style keys without hurting UX/emergency access. Rewrote design v4: BIP39-style 24-word phrase -> MK -> deterministic per-file keys (HKDF(MK,file_id,version)), eliminating wrapped-FK blobs and bulk sync; emergency restore opens any file immediately on cellular; legacy migration background-only and Wi-Fi-first.

2026-11-24: User asked about lost/broken device recovery. Added section 10a to design: account lock vs vault lock, recovery matrix, 3-of-5 Shamir social recovery, optional Argon2id recovery-passphrase envelope (never transmitted), lost-device flow, revocation/rotation semantics.

2026-11-24: v5 maximum-hardening pass: added code-delivery integrity (reproducible signed builds, SRI, isolated asset origin, strict CSP), runtime key hygiene, crypto engineering rules, server hardening, recovery hardening, detection/response, UX-preservation contract, residual risks, implementation priority order.

2026-11-24: User asked for advanced web isolation. Wrote separate spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-web-isolation-design.md: origin topology (app/preview/media/share/api), COOP/COEP/CORP, strict CSP + Trusted Types + Permissions-Policy, sandboxed untrusted-content iframes with no allow-same-origin, crypto worker with per-op tokens, storage partitioning, postMessage discipline, OS/extension limits with native-client fallback, DNS/TLS hardening, verification matrix.

2026-11-24: User asked to integrate web isolation into the security plan. Merged the isolation spec into the canonical design as section 16, updated threat model, hardening layers table, detection, residual risks, verification and priority order. Bumped to v6 INTEGRATED. Marked standalone isolation doc as superseded.

2026-11-24: User asked for even harder plan. v7: replaced deterministic FK (HKDF(MK,file_id)) with per-file random salts so deletion is true crypto-shredding; added key transparency log with witnesses, epoch ratchet for post-compromise security, hardware-bound decrypt mode, duress/travel modes, metadata/traffic defenses, SLSA-style supply chain, mTLS/private infra, safety numbers for recovery contacts, final residual list, updated priority.

2026-11-24: User correctly noted hardware-bound per-decrypt mode is annoying. Reworked §17.3 into three security tiers (Balanced default / High / Maximum opt-in), one-time per-vault choice, configurable touch-cache window, invisible to default users.
